subject: Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) when trying to run BSM

messages.author: a65abcf2d8c47b08
messages.subject: Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) when trying to run BSM
parts:
Hi there, everyone. How are you doing?  Hope fine.

So, I'm working with a group of termites from South America, and I recently ran a ML analysis with DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE and the +j models, and the DEC+j model was the best one. So we tryied to do the BSM with the DEC+j model and we got into a problem.

Your computer has 8 cores. You have chosen to use:
num_cores_to_use = 7 cores for the matrix exponentiations in the likelihood calculations.
Started cluster with 7 cores.
Currently, cluster_already_open=socket cluster with 7 nodes on host ‘localhost’
Detected NON-stratified input. Running get_inputs_for_stochastic_mapping_from_results_object().
Read 13 items
Read 20 items
Read 13 items
Read 20 items
Note: force_sparse is set to TRUE; length(states_list)=1981
Pre-calculating the independent likelihoods on each branch...
Currently, cluster_already_open=socket cluster with 7 nodes on host ‘localhost’
Show Traceback
Rerun with Debug

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 18 nodes produced errors; first error: vectors of negative length are not allowed

The error occours every time we try to run the BSM with the model, and we tested in two different PCs. It tries to run it for a long time, consumes a lot of the RAM, and then some 30 min later it stops and gives this error. Our gest is that our tree has some problems, but we could not indentify it. We ran the ML with optimix = true, speedup = true and force_sparce = true. Is there a solution to this problem?

Thanks.

Cheers.

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) when trying to run BSM
parts:
Hi, not sure what this is. "vectors of negative length are not allowed" is not a BioGeoBEARS error message, it is coming from base R or from the operating system. Googling it suggests:

https://www.google.com/search?q=%22%22vectors+of+negative+length+are+not+allowed%22&oq=%22%22vectors+of+negative+length+are+not+allowed%22&aqs=chrome..69i57.1079j0j7&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8

...that it is some problem with memory allocation.  My best guess is:

1. The Biogeographic Stochastic Mapping algorithm actually doesn't use force_sparse at the moment, this hasn't been programmed (and force_sparse is still a bit experimental, sparse matrix exponentiation (faster for huge matrices) seems to be a bit less stable than standard (slow) dense matrix exponentiation, so it is good to check sparse matrix results against standard dense results.

2. To make the BSM simulations fast-ish, what BSM does is store the dense P matrix for each branch (the P matrix is the result of exponentiating the Q transition matrix).

3. For large trees and/or large matrices, step #2 could take a lot of memory, and eventually fill up memory and lead to a crash like you got.

There is a change I could program the sparse stuff into BSM, but in the immediate future I have a lot of other stuff on my plate.  The main solution then would be to try to shrink your state space and ask if you really need all those states.

Cheers!
Nick
